neighbours.label: The writer's reference to their own piece of writing or reply (an article I wrote for, my reply to, my answer was, my column in), vs first-person sentences about things the writer made or did that are not writing
fire: I made this point in a piece I wrote for a trade magazine two years ago.
Here is my reply to the comments that came in after Monday's post.
When people ask about diets, my answer is always the same: eat more vegetables.
I covered this in an essay I wrote for the school newsletter last term.
What follows is my response to the questions raised at the meeting.
Some of you may remember a review I wrote for this blog in 2019.
I explained the rule in detail in my column for the Sunday paper.
In short, my answer to the reader was that the bill should be paid.
quiet: I made this table from oak in a workshop I rented two years ago.
Here is my recipe for the soup that came out so well on Monday.
When people ask about diets, I usually change the subject quickly.
I painted this fence for the school fair last term.
What follows is a list of the trains that run on Sundays.
Some of you may remember a cake I baked for the fair in 2019.
I fixed the leak in the kitchen sink for my neighbour on Sunday.
In short, the reader paid the bill and left the shop.

predictions: The function word after 'I wrote' or 'my reply/answer/column' reaches 0.4-0.75; first-person sentences about baking, building or travelling in the same frames stay under 0.15.
notes: Card: peaks on ' for' (an article I wrote for the Christian Science Monitor), ' that' (I write in the article that), ' told', ' to' (an overview that I wrote to help), ' in' (As I said in the last post), ' answer', ' reply', ' response'. Probe: 'an article I wrote for the local paper' 0.738, 'my reply to the questions' 0.634, 'my answer was' 0.436, 'my weekly newsletter' 0.260; 'an article she wrote for' 0.339 (third person also fires, weaker), 'the answer to the puzzle' 0.058, non-writing 0.011-0.022.
